name: The Drowned Commission
description:
Beneath four meters of Lake Michigan's encroached shoreline, accessible only by pressurized dive-lock or a corroded service tunnel whose entrance is hidden inside a decommissioned pumping station on the Evanston fringe, lies the Drowned Commission — the partially flooded remains of a major municipal infrastructure hub that once coordinated water treatment, power routing, and emergency services for the original North Shore suburban corridor. The building was sealed and abandoned in 2148 when lake-level projections made continued surface operation untenable, and the official record shows it as demolished. The official record is wrong.

Sometime around 2155, a group of infrastructure salvagers who called themselves the Conduit Collective discovered that the Commission's upper two floors remained above the internal waterline, sustained by a still-functioning emergency bilge system and several intact structural airlocks. They spent five years quietly rehabilitating the accessible space before the first non-salvager was ever permitted inside. Today the Drowned Commission is one of GLMZ's most genuinely off-grid meeting spaces — no Diaspora signal reaches it, no satellite can image it, and the only way in requires either the Collective's escort or knowing which corroded valve in the service tunnel to turn in what sequence.

The interior is a study in controlled decay: walls stripped of anything useful but structurally intact, emergency lighting running off a salvaged microfusion cell, the ever-present sound of water against the outer hull and the occasional groan of pressure differential in the lower floors. The Collective charges access fees in untraceable Φ and maintains a strict neutrality policy — they will host any meeting between any parties so long as no violence occurs on the premises. This rule has been broken twice in the Commission's operational history. Both incidents were resolved by the Collective in ways that are discussed in hushed tones and never elaborated on.

sights: Emergency lighting in amber and red casting long shadows across stripped concrete walls and exposed pipe infrastructure
Waterline staining climbing the lower stairwells in dark bands, each line marking a past high-water event
Condensation running constantly down every surface, pooling in depressions in the floor
Salvaged furniture — mismatched chairs, industrial cable spools repurposed as tables, a cracked municipal conference table still bolted to its original floor
The dive-lock chamber visible through a reinforced porthole, glowing green when pressurized and ready
sounds: The constant low pressure-groan of the hull against lake water, felt as much as heard
The bilge pump cycling every few minutes in a rhythmic mechanical heartbeat
Voices rendered flat and close by the low ceilings and sound-absorbing condensation on every surface
The occasional distant metallic knock from the lower flooded levels — source undetermined and never investigated
smells: Damp concrete, mineral-rich lake water seeping through micro-fractures, and the metallic tang of old plumbing
The faint chemical smell of the bilge treatment compounds keeping the lower levels from becoming toxic
Candle wax and something like machine oil from the Collective's maintenance work
A subtle biological smell from the lower floors that everyone agrees not to discuss
atmosphere.feel: The Drowned Commission imposes a specific psychological state on its visitors: a compression of the social world down to whatever is happening in this room, right now. The complete absence of Diaspora signal is disorienting for most residents of GLMZ, who experience it as a kind of sensory deprivation — BCIs operating in local-only mode, the ambient data stream gone silent. Meetings held here tend to be more direct, more honest, and more tense than meetings held anywhere else. There is also the low, persistent awareness that you are underwater, that the lake is pressing against the walls, and that the Collective — whose members move through this space with complete ease — are the only reason the water stays out.

demographics: The Drowned Commission has no permanent population beyond the six to ten members of the Conduit Collective who maintain and operate it. Visitors are by appointment and introduction only — a cross-section of GLMZ's criminal, corporate, and resistance infrastructure who need a meeting space that does not exist.
economy: The Collective charges a flat access fee of Φ 800 per party per session, payable in advance through a dead-drop system. No recording devices, no weapons above holdout class, and no Diaspora-connected hardware permitted inside. The fee buys the space, the silence, and the Collective's neutrality. The Collective's total operational budget is unknown but is believed to be substantial given the sustained quality of the facility's maintenance.
power_structure: The Conduit Collective operates as a closed collective with a flat internal hierarchy and an external face that presents as monolithic. Leadership is not disclosed to clients. The Collective enforces its own rules through means that have proven sufficient to deter repeat violations. No corponation holds any authority here, and the Collective has thus far successfully resisted multiple attempts to establish leverage over the facility by Ferrogate Security, Arcturus Defense Solutions, and at least one Palladian Group operative.
dangers: Lower floor structural integrity is uncertain — unauthorized descent risks flooding the accessible levels, a fact the Collective enforces with physical barriers and sharp reminders
Complete communication blackout means no emergency contact is possible for the duration of any visit
The Collective's neutrality policy means it will host your enemies as readily as it hosts you, and you may encounter them in the access tunnel
The service tunnel entrance is monitored by parties unknown and has been used at least once for an ambush after a particularly sensitive meeting
Pressure differential events in the dive-lock have caused decompression injuries to visitors who bypassed the Collective's mandatory briefing
opportunities: The only reliably unmonitored meeting space in the Lakeshore Corridor available to non-state actors, making it invaluable for negotiations, handoffs, or conversations that cannot be recorded

The Collective possesses decades of accumulated intelligence about who has met whom here — information they do not sell but occasionally act on in ways that suggest a sophisticated understanding of GLMZ's power landscape
The lower flooded levels contain intact municipal infrastructure archives from the pre-flood era, including records that several powerful entities would pay significantly to acquire or suppress
story_hooks: A meeting was arranged at the Drowned Commission between two factions of a fractured synthetic-personhood resistance cell, brokered by the Collective as neutral ground. One faction never emerged from the service tunnel. The Collective is, unusually, asking for outside help to determine what happened — not because they cannot handle the investigation themselves, but because the answer implicates someone whose identity they cannot afford to know.

Someone has been accessing the lower flooded levels without the Collective's knowledge or permission, and the evidence suggests they have been doing so for months. The Collective wants to know who, how, and what they have found in the municipal archives below — and they are willing to trade access and information to get answers, which tells experienced fixers that what is down there must be genuinely extraordinary.
frequented_by: High-level criminal negotiators requiring neutral and unmonitored ground
Corporate counter-intelligence operatives conducting meetings they cannot log through official channels
Synthetic personhood resistance organizers coordinating sensitive operations
Conduit Collective members maintaining the facility
Rogue ELF intermediaries whose human contacts require off-Diaspora meeting spaces

notable_locations.name: The Neutral Room
notable_locations.description: The primary meeting space — the former emergency coordination center on the second floor, stripped but functional, with the original municipal conference table still bolted down. Seats twelve comfortably and feels like the inside of a pressure vessel.

notable_locations.name: The Dive-Lock
notable_locations.description: The pressurized chamber providing underwater access to the facility for those arriving by submersible or diving equipment. Operated exclusively by the Collective and capable of cycling two people at a time.
